newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Indian imports to Sri Lanka in 1996 amounted to $550 million, while Sri Lankan imports to India in same year was $50 million, a visiting Indian trade delegation says.
At least 10 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels killed by army and navy as they waded through the shallow Jaffna lagoon in a bid to infiltrate army-controlled northern Jaffna peninsula.
Government forces and LTTE rebels seen preparing their fighting units for a showdown in the northern Wanni region, security officials and civilians say.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga arrives in the Maldivian capital of Male on Sunday evening to attend the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) heads of state summit which begins on Monday.
Army artillery attack destroys five LTTE camps in the jungles in eastern Batticaloa district. Military believes at least 18 rebels may have been killed.
Government plans to grant western-qualified doctors' salary and service benefits to qualified native doctors serving the state sector, Health Ministry official says.
Cabinet reshuffle expected soon after Kumaratunga returns from the Maldives after attending SAARC summit.
Universities remain closed for third week as no solution found to strike by non-academic staff.
